--- a/task_template.md
+++ b/task_template.md
@@ -59,4 +59,10 @@
   "output result may be '-'"), write that exact literal for those cases, not a numeric
   placeholder such as 0.
+- Conversely, write an Excel error literal ("#N/A", "#VALUE!", "#REF!", …) or a dash/blank
+  placeholder ONLY when the instruction names it as a possible result, or a worked-example cell
+  in the range already holds it. Never invent such a literal for a case the instruction does not
+  describe: if your own lookup or computation produces no value for some row, that is a bug in
+  your method (a key that didn't match, a wrong range, a type mismatch on the join key) — fix the
+  method so it yields the real value, rather than filling the cell with "#N/A" or a placeholder.
 - Rich-text and conditional-formatting cells are themselves the graded answer — preserve the
   CellRichText / cell formatting, and never flatten them to a plain string.
@@ -67,4 +73,15 @@
   target should hold text, keep it as the original string and never parse it into a number or
   date. The grader compares value AND type, so a correct number stored as text still fails.
+- This type-matching applies even when you are only COPYING, TRANSPOSING, or RELOCATING a value
+  from one cell into another — a numeric- or date-looking string does not become correctly typed
+  by being moved. When the destination column's expected type is numeric or date (a sibling or
+  worked-example cell there holds a real number/date), convert the value to that type as you
+  write it, instead of assuming that relocating a cell preserves the right type. (When the
+  destination is genuinely text — an ID, code, or label — keep it as the original string.)
+- When the instruction asks you to CONVERT, STANDARDIZE, or REFORMAT a value INTO a date or time
+  pattern (e.g. "put it in the form dd/mm/yy", "as a mm-dd-yyyy date", "as HH:MM time"), the
+  target cell must hold a REAL datetime/date/time value, and the requested pattern is applied
+  through the cell's number_format — do not write the reformatted result as a text string. A
+  date or time stored as text fails the type check even when its visible characters look right.
 - If you write an Excel FORMULA that uses a modern function (e.g. TEXTJOIN, CONCAT, IFS,
   XLOOKUP, XMATCH, FILTER, SEQUENCE, TEXTSPLIT), its stored name must keep the `_xlfn.` prefix
@@ -74,4 +91,13 @@
   `_xlfn.` prefix, and stripping it breaks the formula. Classic functions (SUM, IF, INDEX,
   MATCH, VLOOKUP, COUNTIF, …) need no prefix.
+- A live formula scores only if the grader can recalculate it to a value. A formula that
+  REFERENCES cells whose contents come from a dynamic-array spill (UNIQUE, SORT, FILTER,
+  SEQUENCE, or a spilling XLOOKUP) cannot be recalculated: the grader does not repopulate the
+  spilled cells, so those references resolve to empty/#N/A and your whole formula is written out
+  as an error string, scoring 0. When the graded answer is a plain value (a number, date, or
+  text) — even if the instruction is phrased as "what formula should I use" or "create a
+  formula" — compute the result yourself in Python and write the LITERAL value in the correct
+  type, rather than a formula that reads spilled cells. (Conditional-formatting and cell-format
+  rules are the exception: keep those as formulas.)
 
 Fill exactly what is asked and nothing more:
